product_from_film: Vit adds branch, commit, merge and history controls to collaborative video editing inside DaVinci Resolve.
explains_well: The same people and footage from the opening collaboration problem appear in the editor demonstration, connecting the problem to the tool.
unclear: The demo names branches and merges but does not clearly show which person changed what or how competing changes are combined.
scenario: A team waiting on one editor asks for collaboration, then demonstrates Vit branches, commits, merges and history in Resolve.
product_clear_basis: After Resolve integration at 28s and live changes at 32s, the visible Create & Work on Branches label at 34s establishes the collaboration mechanism.

scenes.action: Four people gather around one laptop. Close views and subtitles show impatience about color grading and stitching a file.
scenes.design: Casual live-action room, tilted close-ups and small bottom captions.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 0–14s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: The seated editor asks for a way to collaborate; another person mentions tomorrow’s launch. A large red WHAT ARE text state covers a close-up.
scenes.design: Group reaction shots and oversized red type.
scenes.purpose: Escalate the deadline and collaboration need.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 14–25s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: A dock shows DaVinci Resolve. Its editor opens on the same group footage with a Vit panel and labels Lives On DaVinci Resolve and See Live Changes.
scenes.design: Dark editor, timeline, orange controls and gradient border.
scenes.purpose: Locate the product in an existing workflow.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 25–34s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: A branch-name field and Create control appear. The caption changes to Commit Changes to Vit while timeline and color controls are shown; a commit field and button are emphasized.
scenes.design: Branch controls, timeline, change list and color wheels.
scenes.purpose: Show separate work and saving a version.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 34–43s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: Merge Vit Branches appears beside branch controls. Video states change, then Visualize Vit Graphs accompanies a branching history diagram.
scenes.design: Orange controls, graph nodes and editor preview.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 43–53s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: The editor dims into a small Vit logo on black, followed by creator credits.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 53–61.994s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

sound.detail: The first 27s of draft dialogue broadly matches the subtitles about slow editing, collaboration and a launch deadline, though several words are garbled. Later text is disconnected from the demo and is rejected as product explanation. No validated listening; voice delivery, music, effects and sync remain unknown.
sound.visual_relation: V01,V02 supported by script and captions; V03–V05 rely on visible UI.

categories.finding: Team waits on one editor → deadline pressure → integrated branch/commit/merge demo → history and credits.
A wide group shot around a laptop establishes a team but needs later dialogue to reveal the bottleneck.
Collaborative video editors are the audience; the Resolve panel and branches make the mechanism clear by 34s.
UI crops move between whole editor and controls; labels change for each operation, with a final branching graph. Exact paths and easing are unresolved.
The same group footage moves from the live-action scene into the editor preview, making the demonstration continuous with the setup.
Casual room footage contrasts with a dark editor surrounded by pink-purple-orange gradient borders.
Feature captions are clear, but small branch fields, logs and graph labels are harder to follow in the full interface.
Opening draft dialogue explains the waiting problem and deadline. Later disconnected draft lines are not used as product narration.
categories.reason: ASR and visible subtitles only; no listening.

categories.finding: Music character and structure are unverified.
Effects and their sources are unverified.

categories.finding: Live-action team scenes are reused as the editor’s source material; Resolve is explicitly visible as the integration target, not inferred as the film’s production tool.
Source duration 61.994 s; Watch metadata 1440 × 1080. Frame rate, audio clipping and export quality not checked here.
categories.reason: Parent source metadata supports duration and dimensions; visual review is sampled.

categories.finding: Subtitles preserve the setup and feature labels preserve the demo, but the detailed contribution-to-merge story remains incomplete.
Punch-in views emphasize orange controls, though several logs and panels remain visible around them.
About 25s sets up the problem before roughly 28s of feature demonstration; the merge sequence needs clearer contribution labels.
The request for collaboration is answered by version-control controls, but no explicit team handoff or completed launch is shown.
Impatience and a deadline create a comic problem before the practical demo; audience response is unmeasured.
The opening actors remain recognizable in the preview and timeline, a strong link across the format change.
Branch, commit, merge and graph states are shown. Reliable simultaneous collaboration, conflict resolution and edit preservation were not independently tested.
Git-like operations inside a named video editor and the self-referential team footage make the demo specific.
Make one merge causal and easy to inspect.
categories.experiment: Label one person’s subtitle change and another person’s grade change, then show both retained in the merged preview.

categories.finding: For Tin, show parallel review contributions returning to one asset.
categories.experiment: Use two labeled edits to a campaign draft and a final view that visibly retains both approved changes.

categories.finding: No human new-viewer test was performed.
categories.reason: The product summary is this model’s film-only reading.

categories.finding: Mobile preview and accessibility checks were not performed.
categories.reason: Contact sheets are evidence views, not a stated mobile preview or compliance test.

lessons.keep: Use the opening scene itself as the material in the product demo.
try: Label two separate contributions and show both retained after a merge.
For Tin, merge two approved campaign edits into one clearly labeled final view.
lessons.avoid: Treating operation labels as enough explanation of what a merge actually changes.
lessons.open: Concurrent behavior, conflicts, retained edits, audio and viewer understanding are unverified.
